methods.label: Equate the whole area and the sum of its parts
methods.explanation: The area \((a+b)^2\) of the large square equals the total area \(4\times(ab/2)\) of the 4 triangles plus the area \(c^2\) of the small square. Expanding gives \(a^2+2ab+b^2=2ab+c^2\), so \(a^2+b^2=c^2\).
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses elementary area addition and the Grade 8 perfect-square formula.
